Time: 2 min. Teaching intent: Open the hour and connect it to the week's decision.
Talk track: Produce a reviewable case record that another student can audit from the public source and available export.
Expected answer / misconception: Students can name the outcome.
Visual: The visual previews the physical design or evidence chain.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R5: NIST, Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing | https://www.nist.gov/publications/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing-standardized-approach
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Set the evidence contract.
Talk track: A model-input and assumptions sheet with one uncertainty ranking and next measurement.
Expected answer / misconception: A named artifact with source and a check, not an unsupported opinion.
Visual: Input, reasoning, and evidence are separate.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R5: NIST, Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing | https://www.nist.gov/publications/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing-standardized-approach
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Does a reasonable-looking number become observed evidence?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Provenance, material identity, and measurement conditions are required.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Separate observed input, inferred input, default, and missing field; their evidence strengths differ. Trace the visual in order: observed; inferred / default; missing. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Mark an unspecified CTE curve as missing rather than copying a plausible value from another material system.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Mark an unspecified CTE curve as missing rather than copying a plausible value from another material system. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Pause for an individual answer, then reveal and discuss.
Talk track: Does a reasonable-looking number become observed evidence?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Provenance, material identity, and measurement conditions are required.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A sensitivity comparison changes one declared input while preserving all other comparability conditions. Trace the visual in order: baseline; one change; output difference. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Change a synthetic underfill conductivity from 0.5 to 0.7 W/(m·K) only as an exercise; keep geometry and load fixed. Boundary: Conductivities are synthetic teaching values.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R4: IEEE EPS HIR 2023, Ch. 20: Thermal Management | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/ch20_thermal.pdf
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Change a synthetic underfill conductivity from 0.5 to 0.7 W/(m·K) only as an exercise; keep geometry and load fixed. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. Conductivities are synthetic teaching values.
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Pause for an individual answer, then reveal and discuss.
Talk track: Can the output difference prove the true material value?
Expected answer / misconception: No. It measures model sensitivity under an assumed change, not the actual property.
Visual: The diagram lists the conditions to inspect without marking the answer.
[Sources]
R4: IEEE EPS HIR 2023, Ch. 20: Thermal Management | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/ch20_thermal.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A missing input matters most when plausible variation could reverse the candidate ordering or cross a hard limit. Trace the visual in order: uncertain input; range; decision reversal. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Compare whether interface resistance or minor trace width uncertainty more strongly affects the thermal choice, then prioritize the first measurement.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Pause for an individual answer, then reveal and discuss.
Talk track: Must every uncertain input be measured first?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Prioritize by sensitivity, plausible range, and decision consequence.
Visual: The diagram lists the conditions to inspect without marking the answer.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: The final record states a claim, case revision, conditions, output, uncertainty, and next physical check. Trace the visual in order: bounded claim; traceable record; next check. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: A peer should retrace the comparison from the saved case or export; if a key field is missing, the card says so explicitly.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Pause for an individual answer, then reveal and discuss.
Talk track: What would make the card fail peer review?
Expected answer / misconception: An untraceable number, mismatched conditions, omitted uncertainty, or a claim broader than the evidence.
Visual: The diagram lists the conditions to inspect without marking the answer.
[Sources]
R5: NIST, Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing | https://www.nist.gov/publications/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing-standardized-approach

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Collect or inspect the artifact and bridge to the next hour.
Talk track: A model-input and assumptions sheet with one uncertainty ranking and next measurement.
Expected answer / misconception: Check that the artifact states a source, a constraint, and one unresolved question.
Visual: The three checkpoints summarize the hour's reasoning.
